title: A Clock for the Compass
premise: In the winter of 1917, Rafael Montrose keeps a field hospital ledger of soldiers whose names officers have struck from official records, believing history is something that happens to other people. When a stranger arrives bearing a letter in the unmistakable handwriting of Captain Elias Voss — a man officially dead for eight months — she discovers the 'corpse' has been documenting the very erasures she has been recording in secret. To get his evidence past three checkpoints and into the hands of a war correspondent, Rafael must decide whether loyalty to her hospital, her dead, or the truth matters most. She succeeds at devastating cost: the ledger survives, Voss does not, and Rafael finally accepts that history has been happening to her all along.
about_author: Theo Halloran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed letters from the First World War. They write historical fiction about the people history forgot to write down.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Struck Names
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. In a muddy dressing station near Ypres, Rafael records the names of men erased from official rolls in a hidden ledger, telling herself it is merely a habit, not defiance. A dying soldier asks her to remember him. Emotional beat: quiet, dutiful melancholy — the belief that history happens elsewhere.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. A rain-soaked stranger arrives claiming to deliver medical supplies, but he carries a letter in the handwriting of Captain Elias Voss, officially dead since spring. He asks for someone who 'keeps accounts.' Rafael lies to the matron to hide him. Emotional beat: unease curdling into fascination.

chapters.title: Handwriting of the Dead
chapters.summary: Alternating Rafael and the stranger, Tomas. Tomas reveals Voss is alive, hiding in a canal-side safe house, and has documented the erasures — the same ones in Rafael's ledger. She compares handwriting against letters Voss wrote her hospital years before. Emotional beat: the ground shifting under her certainty.

chapters.title: What the Officers Omit
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, with a flashback to her brother's name vanishing from a casualty list. She realizes her ledger and Voss's evidence are halves of one record, and that Major Aldous — her protector — signed the erasure orders. Emotional beat: betrayal beginning to bloom where loyalty once grew.

chapters.title: The Matron's Warning
chapters.summary: Matron Calloway's POV. Calloway, who has quietly protected Rafael's ledger for months, warns that Aldous suspects a leak and that a courier was arrested at the second checkpoint. She offers Rafael one chance to walk away. Emotional beat: maternal fear and the cost of complicity.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints, One Night
chapters.summary: Rafael and Tomas's POV, alternating. The plan: Rafael will carry Voss's evidence sewn into a wounded man's blanket, passing checkpoints at the canal, the rail yard, and the customs house. The first checkpoint goes wrong; Tomas is detained. Emotional beat: breathless tension and first blood.

chapters.title: Aldous at the Rail Yard
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. At the second checkpoint, Aldous himself inspects the convoy and, recognizing her, offers her a choice: surrender the ledger and be protected, or be erased like the men she records. She sees her brother's name in his orders. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth tearing in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Canal House Burns
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Aldous's men raid the safe house. Voss burns his originals to protect the copies already moving, and is shot covering Tomas's escape. Tomas reaches Rafael with the final page and Voss's last message to her: 'You were the record all along.' Emotional beat: grief as fuel.

chapters.title: The Customs House
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Climax. At the third checkpoint, Rafael trades her own confession — naming Aldous in front of a correspondent and military police — for passage of the evidence. She is arrested as the documents leave her hands, and she lets them go. Emotional beat: triumphant sacrifice, truth chosen over safety.

chapters.title: A Clock for the Compass
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, 1919. Released after the armistice, Rafael reads the published inquiry that vindicates the erased names, her ledger cited as evidence. She visits Voss's grave, plants a compass beside it, and begins a new ledger — this time of names being restored. Emotional beat: belonging found in bearing witness.
